study.notes: STUDY: EUREXA (NCT00359762), open label randomised active comparator trial, exenatide 10 ug twice daily vs glimepiride, both added to metformin, up to 4.5 years; this companion paper (Simo 2015, Cardiovasc Diabetol, open access, Europe PMC PMC4558893, fetched by src/epmc_fetch_one.py into work/fulltext/companion/simo2015_eurexa_hscrp.txt) reports the cardiovascular risk markers, collected as secondary endpoints, at 36 months; the group's own packet holds the two 2012 conference abstracts of the same analyses; n_tx and n_ctrl are the ITT safety population (511 and 508), the number analysed at 36 months is given per row; Table 2 gives LS mean (SE) change from baseline per arm and the treatment difference (SE) with its P value, Table 1 the baseline mean (SD) per arm in the safety population; pct_weight_change -5.67 computed by the session: treatment difference in body weight at 36 months -5.2 kg (Table 2, LS mean -3.9 (0.33) exenatide vs 1.3 (0.32) glimepiride) over the n weighted baseline weight (92.6*511 + 90.9*508)/1019 = 91.75 kg, 100*(-5.2)/91.75 = -5.67; prespecified_endpoint TRUE: the paper states the cardiovascular risk marker data were collected as secondary endpoints; industry_funded TRUE: Eli Lilly and Amylin; the hsCRP row of this trial is in extraction_simo2015_eurexa.csv (earlier extraction), not repeated here

json.design: open label randomised active comparator trial (glimepiride), add on to metformin, secondary analysis of cardiovascular risk markers at 36 months
json.reason: companion full paper of the group's two 2012 abstracts; the six Table 2 markers were not in the 14 marker inventory used for the earlier EUREXA extraction and are added here against the 36 marker inventory

rob.justification: S: the RoB-2 row of EUREXA already in risk_of_bias.csv applies; open label design (D2 high) and 36 month completers of about a third of those randomised (D3) are the concerns; laboratory measured markers at a central laboratory (D4 low)

doubts: treatment differences are printed to one decimal (TC 0.0 with SE 0.08), so the point estimates carry rounding error of up to 0.05 units
n analysed at 36 months is 171 to 203 per arm against 511 and 508 randomised; the LS means come from a repeated measures model but the completer fraction is low
the comparator glimepiride raises body weight, so contrasts are not equivalent to placebo controlled ones (the existing hsCRP row carries the same caveat)
